basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 10.' and it opens 'Vers. 10. Veneruntque ad aream, quae sita est trans Jordanem. Septuaginta dicunt, ad'. The printing's caput is stale here, its marker for this chapter being missing, so the chapter is taken from the lemma, whose best match anywhere in Genesis falls on the very verse the printing numbers.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 10. Veneruntque ad aream, quae sita est trans Jordanem. Septuaginta dicunt, ad aream Adad, qui locus trans Jordanem est, et multis passuum millibus distat ab Abramio, id est a loco ubi Abraham sepultus est. Ergo praetergressi sunt locum ubi sepeliri debebat Jacob, et postea remenso Jordane redierunt ad locum duplicis speluncae. Unde quaeri potest quare hoc fecerint. Sed forte dicet aliquis quod timerent ne bella contra se surgerent, sicut et filii Israel | circumducti sunt quadraginta annis per desertum, donec quadragesimo anno transmisso Jordane venirent in terram promissionis. Sed causa majoris | significantiae hoc factum esse sciamus. In hoc enim loco qui area Adad dicitur, postea multitudo filiorum Israel murmurans contra Dominum igne divino consumpta est. Hoc ergo praesignabat luctus ille vehemens, quo non tantum mors Jacob, quantum ruina illius populi quae ibi futura erat, deflebatur.
